tagline: Gravel through rocky canyons and open valleys beneath the Continental Divide
intro: Big Sheep Creek Back Country Byway runs for more than 50 miles through southwestern Montana, moving from the narrow rock walls of Big Sheep Canyon into broad valley country. BLM suggests three hours for the drive. Most of the route is two-lane gravel; Visit Montana describes a short section of one-lane dirt. BLM highlights the canyon, a valley framed by mountains along the Continental Divide, and the winding Medicine Lodge valley farther north. Visit Montana describes clear, spring-fed creek pools beneath high cliffs, while BLM lists mountain streams, valley bottoms and rock formations among the roadside features. BLM describes it as usually passable for all vehicle types in summer, while warning of hazardous wet surfaces.

The route became a Type I BLM Back Country Byway in 1989. BLM says the road’s type has remained unchanged since that designation. Its designation promotes scenic, recreational and educational travel with minimal infrastructure, consistent with BLM’s backcountry preservation goals.

From Dell, leave I-15 for Westside Frontage Road, then join Big Sheep Creek Road at the beginning of the byway. The route passes Deadwood Campground before reaching Medicine Lodge Road. Turn north through the Medicine Lodge valley to Highway 324, just west of Clark Canyon Reservoir.
notice: Big Sheep Canyon’s high rock cliffs rise above the creek’s clear, deep pools.

moments.title: Dell
moments.text: Dell began as a railway stop and became a trading center for ranchers. The Utah and Northern Railway reached Butte in 1881; Dell’s later connections included a telephone company founded in 1907 to build and maintain a system to Sheep Creek Basin. The settlement lies in a valley beside the Red Rock River. The town’s school opened in 1903 and later became a restaurant, another change of use in this former railway settlement. For the byway, the Dell interchange provides the southern approach, with Westside Frontage Road leading to Big Sheep Creek Road.

moments.title: Big Sheep Canyon
moments.text: The road passes beneath high rock cliffs with views down into Big Sheep Creek’s clear, deep pools. The creek is spring-fed, and Visit Montana singles out the trout visible from a car as one of the drive’s attractions. BLM identifies the canyon’s narrow, rocky walls as one of three distinct geological landscapes on the byway. Beyond comes a broader valley framed by mountains along the Continental Divide. The state tourism account also identifies bighorn sheep and deer as common evening sightings, placing wildlife alongside the water and rock in its description.

moments.title: Medicine Lodge valley
moments.text: Medicine Lodge valley takes its name from the peak above it. A meandering creek shapes this northern part of the byway, following the canyon and the broad valley along the Continental Divide. From the junction with Medicine Lodge Road, BLM gives the remaining northbound drive as roughly 30 miles to Highway 324. The route reaches that highway just west of Clark Canyon Reservoir.

practical: Dell: Parts of the road are impassable when wet. There is no potable water; BLM advises planning fuel stops in advance. (checked 2026-10-11)
